gist: A run of numbered aphoristic notes (28-62) restating the doctrine: the Art perfects the lowest, mineral life in man by fermenting the vital spirit through another life, purifying, dissolving and regenerating it; it glosses images (Walls of Troy, serpent, body of brass, Saturn, Augean Stable) and names the impediments (self-will, evestrum, impure receiving medium).

notes.point: Will alone creates an image; turned to desire for it, will unites with it into a being.
Heart-emotions qualitate the Adepts' powers; essence takes form from Ideas. Forming the humanly producible First Mater from one's own mind for particular ends is true idolatry and talismanic Magic.
Main principle: natural life-fire fermenting the same life in another frees celestial Life and Light. The third principle develops likewise; the fourth is a retrogression.

The spirit teaches its art to the obedient. The imparter of spirit is moved externally, like wind; the receiver of the Afflatus gains universal consciousness. A fermented life passed to another equally fermented makes the patient exceed the agent.

Nature lacks a true conceptive vehicle, so its pure matter is not on earth (Lully); truth needs a pure receiving power, as a true mirror gives true reflection. Plotinus shows how pure matter is generated.

The Art perfects man's third, mineral life, typifying the Divine (Khunrath). We live only the head life; we should be efficient in the medial life, faith; our state is inversion. The Stone (perfected lowest life) answers to Christ (highest).

Hermetism is Light's magnetism by its law, the Wisdom. Nature taken into a will is the Fall. The Art interrogates the Sphinx in man's rational spirit. Linear life must return to a circle (tail-biting serpent).

Troy's walls, built by Apollo's music, figure the insphering of lower life; freeing its center evolves Behmen's Mercurius. Throwing them down is the solution, with noise and fear (Haly, uprooted mineral Tree). The nature then born acts as 'He' through us.
Glosses: body of brass, Hermetic Philosophy (Vaughan), Vegetable spirit. Regeneration evolves the macrocosm's image before the mental eye (Flamel).

Power brings conflict; self-will seeks the mystery for itself. The soul's destiny-dream (evestrum) moves the will; grace, the Divine evestrum, lifts us above it. The mystery exceeds ordinary language.
Mineral life contacts macrocosmic mineral life. The regenerated renounce the head life by sacrifice in faith (Job). Alchemical symbols are more literally true than thought.

Behmen, deepest ontologist, expresses experienced spiritual qualities; the Universal must develop in you. Entering the Signature reveals things in their roots. Mind's speech into pure Ether specificates; mundane Ether holds false forms. Will is the true body, the Salt.
Ontology is emanation from superstantial Light; flat becomes cubic. In Wisdom's Spirit one sees all things' virtues (Solomon, Sendivogius).
Alchemy ferments, purifies and dissolves the vital spirit for regeneration. Seven is rest from ferment. Alchemical elements are those of the Universal Ether, their Quintessence.

The self-begotten life appropriates the hidden Divine Light. The mineral soul first appears as dark vapour, an Augean Stable. Saturn, self-will, is satiated with Rational Light until, like a bursting seed, transmuted. Woman was man's Quintessence.

method.veiled: The Hermetic Art is a perfectioning of the third or lowest or the mineral life in man
method.plain: The material of the work is the lowest of man's lives (called third, lowest or mineral); the Art brings it to perfection, and the perfected result is the Stone.
method.basis: APP ¶44 states it; APP ¶46 identifies the Stone with this life perfected; APP ¶59 restates it.

also.text: the Stone of the Wise is the perfected lowest life, its true consummation, which is mineral in its origin
The third life, the mineral or lowest life in man, brings you into contact with the Macrocosmic mineral life

method.veiled: wheresoever we stand ourselves, there is the relation of the outward life to us itself formed
method.plain: Each level of life in man is related to the corresponding level outside; so working in man's mineral life puts one in contact with the mineral life of the macrocosm.
method.basis: APP ¶59 gives this as the reason ('for') the mineral life contacts the Macrocosmic mineral life.

method.veiled: Alchemy is the art of fermenting the human vital spirit in order to purify it and finally to dissolve it, so that the principle be reconstructed through a regeneration.
method.plain: The whole work in sequence: the human vital spirit is fermented, thereby purified, finally dissolved, and its principle rebuilt in a regeneration.
method.basis: Direct definition in APP ¶68.

method.veiled: The body of brass is the impure natural-born vital spirit.
method.plain: 'Body of brass' names the vital spirit as it is by natural birth, still impure.
method.basis: Direct gloss in APP ¶52.

method.veiled: The fire of the natural life entering into and fermenting the natural fire --- the same life in another --- opens the last, and develops and excites and sets free the celestial Life and Light
method.plain: The natural vital fire of one, entering and fermenting the same vital fire in another, opens that other and releases in it the celestial Life and Light. Atwood calls this 'one main principle'.
method.basis: APP ¶38 states it directly; whether 'another' means another person is left open (see ambiguities).

method.veiled: When one life being fermented throws its life to another equally fermented, a greater perfection is produced in the patient than was before in the agent who imparts it.
method.plain: When life passes from one fermented subject to another equally fermented, the receiver ends more perfected than the giver was; this is how the vital force progresses.
method.basis: APP ¶42: 'That is the law of progression of the Vital force'.

method.veiled: He who imparts the spirit to another is as the wind that blows, moved by an influence external to itself.
method.plain: The one who transmits the spirit is not its source but is moved by an outside influence.
method.basis: APP ¶41 explains the saying 'Ut ventus qui flat, est ille qui dat' this way.

method.veiled: Qui capit, ille sapit
method.plain: The one who receives the Afflatus (the imparted spirit) gains wisdom, because it awakens in him a consciousness related to the universal.
method.basis: APP ¶41: it 'refers to the wisdom imparted by the reception of the Afflatus, since it awakens in him a consciousness related to the universal'.

method.veiled: The spirit teaches its own art, and according as it is obeyed the artist goes on developing the way for him to advance itself to perfection.
method.plain: The spirit itself guides the work; the practitioner's progress depends on obeying it.
method.basis: Direct statement in APP ¶40.

method.veiled: The powers developed, of which the Adepts speak, are produced from emotional sources in the heart, which emotional influences qualitate those powers
method.plain: The Adepts' powers are shaped by heart-emotions such as contrition, purity, mercy and humility; emotion produces essence, which takes its form from the universal Ideas of Nature.
method.basis: APP ¶37: 'Emotion beings forth essence, and essence is qualitated, i.e., specificated, and receives form from Ideas or the universal forms of Nature'.

method.veiled: it is a taking the First Mater which is humanly producible, and forming it finitely and for any particular object or individual end
method.plain: Misuse of the work: giving the humanly producible First Mater a form from one's own mind, for a particular private end, instead of from the universal forms; Atwood calls this true idolatry and the origin of talismanic Magic.
method.basis: APP ¶37: 'in this consists the true idolatry against which the Bible so strongly protests, and that Magic which originated Talismans, Palladia, etc.'

also.text: in lower degree and unlawfully, man may specificate and qualitate from his own mind

method.veiled: The will passing into desire for the image creates it by union with itself into a being
method.plain: Will alone yields only an image; when will turns into desire for that image and unites with it, a real being results.
method.basis: APP ¶36.

also.text: Will creates an image, not a being.

method.veiled: There is no true body but Will; it is the principle of the body --- the Salt.
method.plain: Will is the true principle of body, and this is what 'Salt' names.
method.basis: Direct identification in APP ¶65.

method.veiled: everything depends on the purity of the receiving power
method.plain: Truth is received only through a pure, simple medium of conception that admits nothing foreign, as a true mirror gives a true reflection; ordinary nature has no such medium.
method.basis: APP ¶43: 'you must have a pure conceptive medium; that is true which is conceived simple, without any heterogeneous element'.

also.text: Give a perfectly true mirror, the reflection of objects would be true.

method.veiled: We have no right to be efficient in the present head life; our business is to be efficient in the medial life --- in faith
method.plain: Man ordinarily lives only in the head life; he should act not from it but from the medial life, which is faith, and thereby become effective toward the divine life above. Our present state is inverted.
method.basis: APP ¶45.

also.text: Our present state is one of inversion.

method.veiled: Those who are Hermetically regenerated in this world have given up the Head life or the animal, the rational life
method.plain: The regenerated renounce the animal, rational head life (but not 'the Divine inseeing of the Celestial life') and enter our Lord's life by a sacrifice in faith that they will be restored by Him.
method.basis: APP ¶60; Job's story is called 'a type of that'.

method.veiled: The Art is a question put to Nature respecting the first cause
method.plain: The work is an inquiry into the first cause, addressed not to outward nature but to the spirit in man, which can answer when questioned rationally.
method.basis: APP ¶48: 'To the stronghold of the Sphinx herself in the spirit in man. This spirit being reason-gifted can answer if rationally interrogated.'

also.text: it is an extortion from Protean and Sphynx-like forms of the true answer

method.veiled: the serpent with his tail in his mouth is the chosen illustration of this reduction of the linear into the circular life
method.plain: The tail-biting serpent stands for taking life, which now runs outward in a line, back into its first source as a circle.
method.basis: APP ¶48: 'in other words life has to be taken back into its forst source'.

method.veiled: The Walls of Troy are a figure (and were meant by the poets and traditionalists to be so) of the insphering of the lower life
method.plain: The walls of Troy stand for the enclosing of the lower life within a sphere, done 'in a great resonance'; Apollo, whose music built them, is that life.
method.basis: APP ¶49: 'Apollo is that life, and it is coruscant'.

also.text: Those walls were said to be built by the music of Apollo.

method.veiled: in the setting free of that center, of that coruscation, there is a harmony; what Behmen calls the Mercurius, or spirit of the Sound, is evolved
method.plain: Releasing the flashing center of that life produces a harmony, in which Behmen's Mercurius ('spirit of the Sound') is evolved. The following clause, 'the ether round the sun is compacted and solidified', is not explained here.
method.basis: APP ¶49 states the identification with Behmen's Mercurius; treating it as a sign of the work rests on its place between the insphering (APP ¶49) and the solution (APP ¶50).

method.veiled: The throwing down of the Walls of this is harmony-ensphered life is the Alchemical solution
method.plain: The alchemical 'solution' (dissolution) is the breaking open of that ensphered lower life.
method.basis: Direct identification in APP ¶50.

method.veiled: this also is accompanied with noise, as Haly says
method.plain: The solution is accompanied by noise; in 'another figure', the mineral Tree (roots in the air, summit in the earth) is torn up with a terrible sound and great fear.
method.basis: APP ¶50 states the noise and introduces the Tree as 'another figure' of the same.

also.text: when they are torn from their places a terrible sound is heard and a great fear is felt

method.veiled: when this nature is born in us it asserts itself (or rather, I should say, He asserts Himself, for it is more that It) through us
method.plain: The nature born in the practitioner acts through him as a personal agent ('He') rather than an impersonal force; this chunk does not say who 'He' is.
method.basis: APP ¶51 alone; 'this nature' is read as what follows the solution of APP ¶50.

method.veiled: The Hermetic Philosophy is a process of experimentation into the Universal Spirit through man
method.plain: The work is an experiment carried out in and through man, by which a particular spirit is joined to the universal spirit.
method.basis: APP ¶53: 'the art by which a particular spirit (to use Vaughan’s words) is allied to the universal'.

also.text: Hermetism is the magnetism of Light according to its own law

method.veiled: is evolved before the mental eye in the recreative process of the regeneration
method.plain: During regeneration the whole image of the macrocosm, typified in man the microcosm, unfolds before inner sight.
method.basis: APP ¶55.

method.veiled: In the work, wherever there is power there is a conflict: the multitudinous enemies try to rush in
method.plain: Wherever power develops in the work, opposing forces press in, and the self-willed spirit tries to seize the mystery for itself with lures; the enemies are not otherwise identified.
method.basis: APP ¶56.

also.text: the self-willed spirit endeavors to gain the mystery and offers all its lures in order to get the end for itself

method.veiled: we may rise above this evestrum, as Paracelsus calls it
method.plain: The 'evestrum' is the dream of its whole afterlife, its destiny, with which the soul enters the body; it supplies motives to a will that does not see beyond it, and is seldom passed except by God's grace, called the Divine evestrum.
method.basis: APP ¶57: 'unless moved by God’s grace (the Divine evestrum, relatively to man), and so are enabled to overcome it'.

method.veiled: you must have the Universal developed in you before you can understand the Universal
method.plain: Understanding of the universal comes only from having it developed within oneself; Behmen's terms (hardness, enclosing, coldness, attraction, compunction) record such inner experience of spiritual qualities.
method.basis: APP ¶65: such words are 'expressive, as far as such an instrument can be, of internal knowledge and consciousness'.

method.veiled: The speech of Mind uttered into the pure Ether qualitates and specificates.
method.plain: Mind gives specific form by 'speaking' into the pure Ether, which is connected with the supersensual life, not into the mundane Ether, which is full of false forms.
method.basis: APP ¶64 states the act and the two-fold Ether.

method.veiled: When an entrance is effected into the Signature, then there is a clearing of the understanding
method.plain: Entering 'the Signature' (not defined here) clears the understanding to see the life in the Divine Wisdom and to know things in their roots; likewise one who finds the Wisdom and looks out in its Spirit sees the nature and virtues of all things.
method.basis: APP ¶63 states the result of entering the Signature without defining it; linking it with APP ¶67 (finding the Wisdom) is an inference from the parallel outcome.

also.text: If you find the Wisdom, and coming out in the Spirit of Wisdom, look into the world, then you may see as Solomon did the nature and virtues of all things.

method.veiled: The Alchemical symbols, phrases, metaphors, which so disguise the art are more than what they seem; they point out a reality
method.plain: The disguising symbols refer to something real and would prove more literally true than supposed to one in their spirit.
method.basis: APP ¶61.

method.veiled: The great principle of the number seven is a Rest from the ferment or action of the Vitalizing or Divine principles.
method.plain: Seven signifies rest after the fermenting action of the vitalizing or Divine principles.
method.basis: Direct statement in APP ¶69.

method.veiled: When speaking of the four elements, Alchemists refer to the four elements of the Universal Ether.
method.plain: The alchemists' 'four elements' are four principles of the Universal Ether, which is their quintessence and 'the Quintessence of both worlds'.
method.basis: APP ¶69.

method.veiled: The Divine Light, the Essence of Gold, is hidden in the self-begotten life.
method.plain: The 'gold' sought is the Divine Light, concealed within man's own self-begotten life.
method.basis: Direct identification in APP ¶70.

method.veiled: This life of ours, instead of administering to the Divine Life, appropriates it.
method.plain: Our self-begotten life takes the Divine Life for itself instead of serving it.
method.basis: APP ¶70.

method.veiled: when first seen by introspection, is as a dark vapour, monstrum, horrendum, informe, ingens, cui lumen ademptum
method.plain: On first inward view the mineral soul (lowest life) appears as a dark, shapeless, monstrous vapour; its cleansing is a Herculean labour, the Augean Stable.
method.basis: APP ¶71 identifies the mineral soul seen by introspection with this vapour and with the Augean Stable.

also.text: it is the Augean Stable the cleansing of which involved Hercules in so much labour

method.veiled: Saturn or the self-willed life
method.plain: 'Saturn' names the self-willed life in man, which first traps the Light and then craves more to feed what it has trapped.
method.basis: APP ¶72: 'He first of all entraps the Light, and then he longs for more to feed that center which he has entrapped'.

method.veiled: he must be given from without plenty "of the honey of the bees", the aurific seed, the Rational Light
method.plain: The self-willed life is overcome not by force but by satiation: it is fed abundantly, from outside, with the Rational Light (also called 'honey of the bees' and 'aurific seed').
method.basis: APP ¶72: 'can only be overcome in the process by satiation'.

also.text: Saturn or the self-willed life can only be overcome in the process by satiation

method.veiled: the selfish Saturnine life in man when once it has passed into its new life, or rather admitted it, assimilates that life into itself and becomes itself transmuted
method.plain: Fed with Light, the selfish life grows past itself, as a seed bursts its husk into flower and grows for another generation, and is transmuted.
method.basis: APP ¶72 gives the seed comparison explicitly.

a perfectioning of the third or lowest or the mineral life in man

equivalences.quote: the Head life or the animal, the rational life

quotes.text: We live in but one life, the head life, but there are three possible lives

equivalences.quote: efficient in the medial life --- in faith

quotes.text: either in the sensible, the perceptive, or the power life; this last conjoined to the other two makes them efficient

terms.meaning: Our present state.

quotes.text: Our present state is one of inversion.

quotes.text: a development of the art by which a particular spirit (to use Vaughan’s words) is allied to the universal

terms.meaning: The magnetism of Light according to its own law; that Law is its emanating spirit, called wisdom.

equivalences.quote: Hermetism is the magnetism of Light according to its own law

terms.meaning: The Law of Light, its emanating spirit; in its Spirit one may see the nature and virtues of all things.

equivalences.quote: which Law is its emanating spirit called wisdom, for it is the Wisdom

quotes.text: If you find the Wisdom, and coming out in the Spirit of Wisdom, look into the world

terms.meaning: The art of fermenting the human vital spirit to purify it and finally dissolve it, so that the principle is reconstructed through a regeneration.

equivalences.quote: The throwing down of the Walls of this is harmony-ensphered life is the Alchemical solution

terms.meaning: The enclosing of the lower life, figured by the Walls of Troy, done in a great resonance.

terms.meaning: The flashing center of the lower life (Apollo); its setting free produces harmony.

quotes.text: Apollo is that life, and it is coruscant

equivalences.quote: what Behmen calls the Mercurius, or spirit of the Sound, is evolved

terms.meaning: The impure natural-born vital spirit.

equivalences.quote: The body of brass is the impure natural-born vital spirit.

terms.meaning: Man's life-spirit; impure as naturally born; what Alchemy ferments, purifies and dissolves.

quotes.text: the human vital spirit

terms.meaning: The life passed between fermented lives; it progresses by transmission from agent to patient.

quotes.text: That is the law of progression of the Vital force

terms.meaning: The growth-causing spirit, predominant in the vegetable kingdom.

equivalences.quote: The Vegetable spirit is the growth-causing spirit

terms.meaning: The vital fire of the natural life; fermented by the same life from another, it is opened and frees the celestial Life and Light.

quotes.text: sets free the celestial Life and Light

terms.meaning: The action of one life on another (or on the vital spirit) that opens it and frees a higher life; also the action of the Vitalizing or Divine principles, from which seven is a rest.

quotes.text: When one life being fermented throws its life to another equally fermented
a Rest from the ferment or action of the Vitalizing or Divine principles

terms.meaning: The imparted spirit whose reception gives wisdom by awakening a consciousness related to the universal.

quotes.text: the wisdom imparted by the reception of the Afflatus

terms.meaning: To give specific quality and form; essence is qualitated by Ideas, and the speech of Mind qualitates in the pure Ether.

terms.meaning: That from which essence receives form.

equivalences.quote: Ideas or the universal forms of Nature

terms.meaning: In a special sense: man specificating and qualitating from his own mind, forming the First Mater for a particular end.

quotes.text: in this consists the true idolatry against which the Bible so strongly protests

terms.meaning: The receiving medium through which universal principles are conceived; nature lacks a true one; it must be pure and simple for truth.

quotes.text: There is no such thing as truth absolute in nature, because she has no true conceptive vehicle
Thus everything depends on the purity of the receiving power.

terms.meaning: Not to be found on earth (Lully); Plotinus shows how it is generated.

equivalences.with: quintessence of the four principles called elements
equivalences.quote: This Ether is a quintessence of those very four principles, which they call elements.
It is the Quintessence of both worlds.

quotes.text: The Ether is two-fold: the mundane, which is full of the false forms; the pure, which is not of this world

terms.meaning: In alchemical usage, the four elements (principles) of the Universal Ether.

equivalences.with: four elements of the Universal Ether
equivalences.quote: Alchemists refer to the four elements of the Universal Ether

terms.meaning: The essence of a whole: the Ether of the four elements and of both worlds; man of the whole creation; woman of man.

quotes.text: As man was the Quintessence of the whole creation, so woman was the Quintessence of man --- the love-spirit was in her.

terms.meaning: The principle of the body, which is Will.

terms.meaning: Creates an image, not a being; passing into desire for the image it unites with it into a being. The only true body.

quotes.text: the soul comes into this body with the dream of its whole afterlife presented to it
God’s grace (the Divine evestrum, relatively to man)

sources.name: Behmen
sources.use: His Mercurius, or spirit of the Sound, cited for the harmony freed from the lower life; called the deepest writer on ontological subjects, less scientific than the Platonists but more descriptive, awakening, suggestive; his three primary forms and doctrine of the Absolute Will read as expressions of conscious experience of the creative mystery. Endorsed.

sources.name: Behmen
sources.quote: through the principle in the sound with the voice
sources.use: Supports (chap. I, 1) knowledge of things in their roots, 'out of their essence', on entering the Signature; his words hardness, enclosing, coldness, attraction, compunction (Ch. II, 12) read as expressing spiritual emotions known inwardly.

ambiguities.basis: It stands in a list of heart-emotions; the text gives no other sense for 'live' there.

readings: another person: vital fire passed between two people
another seat or vessel of the same life, not specified as a person
ambiguities.basis: Person: APP ¶41 'He who imparts the spirit to another' and APP ¶42 'patient' and 'agent'. APP ¶38 itself does not say a person is meant.

ambiguities.quote: The fourth contrariwise; it is a procreation of the third through the second --- a retrogression.
readings: a separate numbered series of principles, of which APP ¶38 gives 'one main principle', with the first and second not given here
the numbered lives of APP ¶44-45/¶59 (third = mineral life, second possibly the medial life)
ambiguities.basis: APP ¶39 opens 'The third principle is developed in like manner' after APP ¶38's unnumbered 'one main principle'; APP ¶44 and ¶59 use 'third' for the mineral life, and APP ¶45 names a 'medial' life. No identification is stated.

ambiguities.quote: either in the sensible, the perceptive, or the power life
readings: corresponds to the mineral/vegetable/animal lives of APP ¶59
corresponds to the head, medial and divine lives named later in APP ¶45
a separate triad not mapped onto either
ambiguities.basis: APP ¶45 lists both triads in one paragraph without equating them; APP ¶59-60 call the head life animal/rational and rank vegetable and animal above mineral.

ambiguities.quote: Nature has taken from the primal source into a will is the history of the Fall.
readings: '[That] Nature has [been] taken from the primal source into a will' is the Fall
Nature has taken [something] from the primal source into a will of its own, and this is the Fall
ambiguities.basis: The sentence is grammatically incomplete as printed; APP ¶70 and ¶72 speak of the self-begotten, self-willed life appropriating the Divine, consistent with either.

ambiguities.quote: the ether round the sun is compacted and solidified
readings: an outward cosmic effect of the inner harmony
a figure for the inner 'sun' (Apollo, 'that life') being given a body
ambiguities.basis: APP ¶49 identifies Apollo with 'that life' and places this clause after the freeing of its center; no further explanation is given.

ambiguities.quote: He asserts Himself, for it is more that It
readings: 'He' personifies the nature born in us, without further identification
ambiguities.basis: APP ¶51 corrects 'it' to 'He' without naming the referent; APP ¶46 and ¶60 associate the work with 'our Lord'.

ambiguities.quote: they renounce a word, their life is sealed in another Covenant
readings: 'a word' as printed (some utterance or vow)
ambiguities.basis: The same paragraph speaks of those 'in this world' cutting themselves off from the head life; the text gives no clarification.

translations.original: Ut ventus qui flat, est ille qui dat
translations.translation: As the wind that blows, so is he who gives.
He who receives, he is wise.
Thus one goes to the stars!

translations.original: monstrum, horrendum, informe, ingens, cui lumen ademptum
translations.translation: a monster, dreadful, shapeless, huge, deprived of light

threads.note: The notes are numbered (28) to (62), continuing a numbered series begun before this chunk.
'The third principle is developed in like manner' and 'The fourth contrariwise' presuppose an enumeration of principles (first, second) not given here.
'You may find out in Plotinus how that pure matter is generated' points to Plotinus.
'Compare also the Chaldaic Oracles (Article Hecate, etc.)' points to a reference on Hecate.
Points to Hermes' Golden Treatise, cap. 4.
'of the honey of the bees' is set in quotation marks without attribution, pointing to an unnamed source.
